verdict.rationale: Crossplane's control plane continuously reconciles desired state in the background and automatically corrects drift. Users configure that behavior declaratively through function pipelines instead of writing controllers, so it is a real but narrow form of autonomous background automation. It is not evidenced as a general-purpose automation facility: there is no documented scheduling (recurring/cron jobs) or arbitrary event-triggered workflows. Missing for 10: user-defined scheduled or event-triggered automations, documentation of background automation beyond state reconciliation, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: If your software ever drifts from your desired state, the control plane automatically corrects the drift.
With Crossplane you don't have to write a controller. Instead you configure a pipeline of functions. The functions return declarative configuration that Crossplane should apply.
Crossplane's key value is that it unlocks the benefits of building your own Kubernetes custom resources without having to write controllers for them.
